Yes, gold does rust in water. Rusting is the process by which metals, especially those made of iron or steel, lose their shine and gradually deteriorate over time. It occurs when oxygen and moisture are present in the environment, causing oxidation of the metal.

When gold comes into contact with water, it reacts with the oxygen in the air to form a protective oxide layer called galvanic corrosion (also known as anodic corrosion). This protective layer helps to prevent further rusting by providing a barrier against further oxygen and moisture from coming into contact with the gold.

The process of rusting can be slowed down or prevented by using methods such as cleaning the metal, maintaining its cleanliness, and exposing it to pure air without water.
